candidates.title: Sample Count Is Not Enough: Candidate-Generation Strategy Shapes the Energy and Performance of LLM Test-Time Scaling
candidates.date_evidence: arXiv submission history lists v1 only. The secondary index's September 18 'Last Updated' is not an arXiv revision; a guessed v2 HTML endpoint returned an error and was discarded.
candidates.old_bottleneck: T5 distinguishes sample counts from real budgets, but lacked a controlled example separating candidate count from execution scheduling.
candidates.mechanism: Hold eight candidates fixed and vary sequential call count versus batch size.
candidates.evidence_conditions: Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct; fixed-N GSM8K study uses A100-SXM4 80GB, 100 prompts × 3 repetitions, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, 512-token cap. Logical output volumes differ by no more than 1%; schedules sample independently. Ratios in Table VI compare serial 8×1 to batched 1×8: 4.64–4.86 energy, 5.77–6.12 P95 latency.
candidates.limitation: Gross GPU-device energy includes idle power during the interval, not whole-node energy. Loading/warm-up/final grading excluded. No FLOPs equivalence or mechanism isolation; limited models, hardware and Hugging Face batch generation. Continuous serving and dependent search are not tested.
candidates.decision: Added one concise, matched paragraph to Chinese and English T5 §3; source record supplied separately for root integration.

candidates.title: FlowBalance: Verifier-Grounded Self-Improvement from On-Policy Reasoning Experience
candidates.reading_depth: Abstract, §4.1/4.4 propositions and §5.1–5.2 setup/table targeted; no complete appendix or code audit.
candidates.old_bottleneck: Sparse outcome feedback and dense same-model guidance can reinforce incorrect trajectories.
candidates.mechanism: Use verifier-derived group-advantage sign to retain, reverse or disable privileged self-guidance, then fit a normalized response target through trajectory balance.
candidates.evidence_conditions: Qwen3-4B/8B; common prompts, group size, verifier, length cap and evaluation within each backbone. Step-180 results over five seeds; AIME24 uses pass@16 whereas four other tests use pass@1.
candidates.limitation: Training-time scoring sees solutions or task feedback; not information-free self-improvement. Theory conditions on realized groups and stopped scores. Averaged benchmarks mix pass@k protocols; independent reproduction and complete compute accounting not checked.
candidates.decision: Candidate only. Mechanistic extension of T4 self-feedback/verifier branch; does not presently require changing the existing narrative.

candidates.title: GraphAHA: Graph-Based Adaptive Search with Heterogeneous Actions for Test-Time Code Generation
candidates.reading_depth: Canonical graph, score backup, experimental setup, Table 2 and budget analysis targeted; code not reproduced.
candidates.old_bottleneck: Tree search duplicates equivalent program states and cannot share evaluations across convergent paths.
candidates.mechanism: AST-normalized exact state merging in a DAG plus hierarchical Thompson sampling over sampling, repair and sketch/implementation actions.
candidates.evidence_conditions: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct and DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct; 223 LiveCodeBench and 165 CodeContests problems, 32 calls, three seeds, temperature 1.0. Public-test and held-out correctness are separate; token-normalized curves also reported.
candidates.limitation: The headline average gain concerns visible-test P-Pass@1. On Qwen LiveCodeBench, hidden-inclusive Pass@1 trails AB-MCTS by 2.1 points despite stronger public-test results. Low-budget performance initially trails sampling; calls/tokens are not measured energy or FLOPs.
candidates.decision: Candidate only; useful conditional counterexample to equating public verifier improvement with final correctness, but no main-text change this run.

candidates.title: Scaling Discovery through Test-Time Communication
candidates.reading_depth: Abstract, contributions, §2/Table 1 and budget/feedback qualification targeted; not full 34-page or code audit.
candidates.old_bottleneck: Independent candidate generation cannot reuse another agent's intermediate discoveries; communication may introduce coordination overhead.
candidates.mechanism: Identical agents share a workspace and verified-progress records while preserving distinct exploratory approaches.
candidates.evidence_conditions: ARC-AGI-3, polyomino packing and MNIST compression use task-specific action or per-agent time budgets; a Terminal-Bench 2.0 comparison shows team@2 does not beat pass@2.
candidates.limitation: Benefits depend on sufficient budget and useful progress feedback. Per-agent time/action budgets are not a universal total-token/FLOPs comparison; finite single-agent failures do not prove zero support.
candidates.decision: Candidate only; potential later T5 extension after full protocol/cost audit, not evidence of a universal multi-agent scaling law.

candidates.title: Rethinking RL for LLM Reasoning: It's Sparse Policy Selection, Not Capability Learning
candidates.reading_depth: Version history, §5 objective and mixed-success filtering, Table 3 cost notes and §6 discussion targeted.
candidates.old_bottleneck: Pass@1 gains alone do not identify whether RL introduces new strategies or changes probabilities.
candidates.mechanism: Entropy-gated contrastive updates target sparse decision points using offline mixed-success rollouts.
candidates.evidence_conditions: Comparisons with released RL checkpoints across multiple mathematical benchmarks; Table 3 includes estimated costs derived from published scripts at RunPod prices.
candidates.limitation: Title is stronger than a universal conclusion supported by finite task/model tests. Costs are not uniformly measured matched end-to-end runs; data and training pipelines differ. No v2/v3 diff was completed, so the substantive revision content remains unverified.
candidates.decision: Revision-in-window candidate only; not a September first publication and not a verified new correction of prior results.
